description: Roman villa site, known from limited excavations. Coins from the southern wing suggest it was constructed around 300 CE, but the rest of the villa is undated. A semi-circular structure located around a nearby spring was suggested to be a possible nymphaeum.
bibliography: Martyn, Blick, Brindle, and et al. “Whatley Combe, Nunney (Somerset).” The Rural Settlement of Roman Britain: an online resource, 2015. https://doi.org/10.5284/1030449.
Stead. “A Roman Villa at Whatley Combe, Nunney, Somerset.” Somerset Archaeology and Natural History 114 (1979).
